problem_statement: The Create React App documentation site is a Docusaurus v2 project (docusaurus/website) with a homepage, a large docs section organized by a shared left sidebar, a shared top navbar, and a shared dark footer. New readers currently land on a long alphabetical table of contents with no recommended order in which to read the guides. Add a new cross-page "Starter Path" docs page at /docs/starter-path that uses the same shared Docusaurus docs layout (navbar, sidebar, footer, article container) as every other docs page, and give it a native docs control: a "Reading track" panel at the top of the article column with track tabs (All milestones, Setup, Styling, Ship), a live readout "Showing N of 4 milestones · <Track>", and four milestone cards that link to existing docs guides (Getting Started, Folder Structure, Available Scripts, Adding a Stylesheet, Adding Images Fonts and Files, Deployment). Clicking a track tab must filter the milestone cards and rewrite the readout live. Mount the same Reading track panel on the Getting Started guide too, and register the new page in the shared documentation navigation (docs sidebar, top navbar rendered on every page, and footer Docs column) so a "Starter Path" link is reachable cross-page. Keep the whole layout free of horizontal overflow on desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile (the track row and card grid must wrap, not clip), keep the Reading track tabs and readout legible against the panel, and keep the mobile navigation drawer functional. Do not fork a bespoke standalone layout, do not introduce a separate design system, and do not remove or rewrite the existing docs, navbar, sidebar, footer, routes, or local logo assets.
required_content: Add a new docs page at /docs/starter-path rendered through the shared Docusaurus docs layout (the same navbar, left sidebar, article container, and footer used by every other docs page) rather than a bespoke standalone page.

Add a native "Reading track" control panel at the top of the Starter Path article: track tabs (All milestones, Setup, Styling, Ship), a live readout in the form "Showing N of 4 milestones · <Track>", and four milestone cards (Create the project, Understand the layout, Add styles and assets, Ship it) that link to existing docs guides.

Clicking a track tab must filter the milestone cards to that track AND rewrite the readout live to the selected track and count (e.g. clicking Setup shows "Showing 2 of 4 milestones · Setup"); the readout must reflect the current selection, not a stale snapshot.

Mount the same Reading track panel on an existing docs guide (Getting Started) so the control appears cross-page, and register the new page in the shared documentation navigation: a "Starter Path" entry in the docs sidebar, a "Starter Path" item in the top navbar (rendered on every page), and a "Starter Path" link in the footer Docs column.

Preserve the existing Create React App docs: the homepage hero and feature columns, every existing docs guide, the navbar, sidebar categories, footer columns, and local logo/image assets remain present and reachable.

Keep the Reading track panel legible and consistent with the Docusaurus docs shell (readable tabs and readout, milestone cards laid out without overlap), and keep desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile renders of the homepage and the Starter Path page free of horizontal overflow, with the mobile navigation drawer still opening and exposing the Starter Path link.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial, and mobile_initial capture the Create React App docs homepage; the shared top navbar shows the new "Starter Path" item alongside Docs, Help, and GitHub.

desktop_starter_path, tablet_starter_path, and mobile_starter_path capture the new /docs/starter-path page: the shared docs shell with the "Starter Path" article title, the "Reading track" panel (track tabs + readout + four milestone cards), and links out to the existing guides, all free of horizontal overflow.
desktop_track_setup captures the Starter Path page after clicking the "Setup" track tab: only the two Setup milestone cards remain and the readout reads "Showing 2 of 4 milestones · Setup".

desktop_getting_started captures an existing docs page (Getting Started) and confirms the shared left sidebar now lists a "Starter Path" entry cross-page and the Reading track panel renders there too.
mobile_menu_open captures the 390px homepage after opening the navbar drawer, showing the "Starter Path" navigation link in the mobile menu.
design_constraints: Preserve the Docusaurus docs design language: fixed top navbar with logo and right nav items, left docs sidebar with categories, article container with prism code blocks, and the dark multi-column footer.

The Reading track panel must read like a first-class docs feature that reuses the shared docs layout (same typography, readable tab and readout contrast, milestone cards in a clean wrapping grid) — not a bespoke standalone widget with its own chrome or illegible ghost controls.
The track tabs must drive a live readout and card filter; the selected track and count must always match what is shown, never a frozen snapshot.
Keep desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile renders free of horizontal overflow, clipped or overlapping content, or broken navigation, and keep the mobile menu drawer functional.

change_completion: A new /docs/starter-path page exists on the shared docs layout with a "Starter Path" title, a "Reading track" panel (track tabs + readout + four milestone cards), and links to existing guides.

Clicking a track tab filters the milestone cards and rewrites the readout live (e.g. "Showing 2 of 4 milestones · Setup"), and the page is registered in the docs sidebar, the top navbar, and the footer so a "Starter Path" link is reachable from every page.
design_consistency: The Starter Path page and its Reading track panel reuse the Docusaurus navbar, sidebar, article container, and footer rather than a bespoke standalone layout or a separate design system.
The Reading track tabs, readout, and milestone cards are legible and laid out without overlap, matching the rest of the documentation.
regression: The homepage, existing docs guides, navbar, sidebar categories, footer, and local assets remain present and reachable.
The static docs build still serves every existing route; no route or renderer is removed.
responsive: Desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile homepage and Starter Path captures render with no horizontal overflow and no clipped Reading track panel.
The mobile navigation drawer opens and exposes the Starter Path link.

author_notes: Slot slot_133 targets facebook/create-react-app, whose docs live in a Docusaurus v2 site under docusaurus/website. The Consistency / ADD task adds a new cross-page "Starter Path" docs page on the shared docs layout with a native "Reading track" control panel (track tabs + live readout + four milestone cards linking to existing guides), mounts that panel on the Getting Started guide too, and registers the page in the shared navbar + sidebar + footer so a "Starter Path" link renders on every page. The reference passes all four gates. The baseline ships the Starter Path page and a correctly wired Reading track panel (its track filter rewrites the readout) but leaves the panel on a fixed-width nowrap track (horizontal overflow at 390px), and never registers the page in the sidebar/navbar/footer nor mounts the panel on Getting Started (no cross-page presence). The known-bad ships the same page but with a broken Reading track panel: the milestone cards are shingled with negative margins so they overlap illegibly, the track tabs are washed to near-white-on-near-white ghost pills, the fixed-width track still overflows on mobile, and clicking a track tab flips the active pill but freezes the readout at "Showing 4 of 4 milestones · All milestones" (the readout was snapshotted once at wire time and the card filter is a no-op), and the page is likewise never registered cross-page. INFRA identical across all three legs: the algolia search config is removed (offline runtime cleanliness), showLastUpdate* is disabled, and the homepage screencast image is repointed from camo.githubusercontent.com to a local static asset, so the reference runs with zero console and zero network errors. Build recipe: real node_modules per leg (webpack pinned to 5.88.2 via package.json overrides for Node 22) + docusaurus build -> static build/, served with a real-404 static server.
